drug_class: HER2-targeted monoclonal antibody combination (with subcutaneous delivery enzyme)
purpose: This medicine is used to treat a type of breast cancer that has too much of a protein called HER2. It is used in adults with early-stage or advanced (metastatic) HER2-positive breast cancer. It is usually given along with chemotherapy as part of your treatment plan.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have too many HER2 receptors on their surface, which helps the cancer grow. This medicine contains two targeted proteins — pertuzumab and trastuzumab — that attach to HER2 receptors and block the signals that tell cancer cells to grow and multiply. The hyaluronidase ingredient helps the medicine absorb quickly under your skin so it can be given as a shot instead of a long IV infusion.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, tiredness or fatigue, hair loss, injection site reactions (like redness or irritation where the shot is given), low white blood cell counts (which can raise infection risk), muscle or joint aches, and numbness or tingling in the hands or feet.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart problems, so your doctor will check your heart regularly during treatment. It must NOT be used during pregnancy because it can harm or even cause the death of an unborn baby — use reliable birth control during and for 7 months after treatment. Tell your doctor right away if you have shortness of breath, swelling, or a rapid or irregular heartbeat. Serious allergic or infusion-like reactions can also happen, especially during or shortly after the injection.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) under the skin, usually in the thigh. It is typically given once every 3 weeks (every 21 days) by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital setting. The dose is already pre-mixed in a fixed combination, so your care team will determine the right schedule and number of cycles for your specific treatment plan.
